findings.claim: "The discipline is sequence — the handbook holds the order because Now-What decisions land badly when the data and pattern questions have not been answered."
findings.failure_mode: rationale attributed to the handbook that it does not give
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 113 says only that the questions are asked "in the following order". Source lines 1721-1725: "At the conclusion, or sometimes in the middle, of a meeting it is very useful to ask the following questions in the following order" — no reason for the order is stated.
findings.fix: correct: The handbook asks the three questions "in the following order"; hold the sequence so the group answers What and So What before Now What.

findings.fix: correct: "...It is a danger signal telling you that your development and implementation process is missing the essential ingredient of involving all who should be involved." [V]

findings.claim: An action closed as "we'll look into it" diagnosed as "buy-in rather than ownership"
findings.failure_mode: concept misapplied: vague commitment is not the handbook's buy-in
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 17: buy-in = someone else did the development and deciding and now must convince you to implement it. A vague, unowned action is a different failure.
findings.fix: correct: Now-What phase without named owner and date — no one has taken ownership of the action

findings.fix: correct: "Where do you have freedom to act? What's in your 15%?" [V]

findings.claim: "The contributory-factor analysis needs to name a structural paradox, not solve it — Wicked Questions is the move."
findings.failure_mode: function narrowed against the source
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 89: wicked questions' value lies in their capacity "to open up options, inquiry and bring to the surface the fundamental issues that need to be addressed"; source lines 1368-1369 add they can be used "to find creative alternatives for stubborn problems". The handbook does not say they are not to be solved.
findings.fix: correct: The contributory-factor analysis needs to surface a structural paradox that has no obvious answer — Wicked Questions is the move.

findings.claim: The wicked question is "a genuine paradox, not a solvable problem"
findings.failure_mode: overstates the source's definition
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 89: wicked questions "do not have obvious answers"; nothing says they are unsolvable.
findings.fix: correct: a genuine paradox with no obvious answer

findings.claim: "Surfacing a wicked tension and treating it as a solvable problem — solved by naming it as a Wicked Question rather than reaching for a single answer."
findings.failure_mode: overstates the source's definition
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 89; source lines 1368-1375 frame wicked questions as opening options and finding creative alternatives, not as unsolvable.
findings.fix: correct: Surfacing a wicked tension and reaching for an obvious answer — solved by naming it as a Wicked Question and opening up options.

findings.claim: Window-dressing invitations "solved by the Nothing About Me Without Me discipline"
findings.failure_mode: mis-cited section
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 45 places the window-dressing caveat in "Engage the Unusual Suspects" (source lines 499-501), not "Nothing About Me Without Me".
findings.fix: correct: solved by the Engage the Unusual Suspects discipline (craft an invitation that is authentic and welcoming) applied at Phase 0

findings.claim: "this source's 5 Whys and TRIZ are the facilitation-layer complements that surface the network structure"
findings.failure_mode: relationship to another source loosened; tension omitted
findings.evidence: Handbook deep ref line 87: 5 Whys' original goal was "to determine the root cause". LFUO deep ref lines 57, 91, 306: LFUO departs from root-cause analysis, and its own sensemaking tool for the Lessons Learned Analysis is the Five Hows (lines 145-151). Presenting 5 Whys as a complement without naming that tension misstates the fit.
findings.fix: correct: LFUO provides the networked-causality epistemology and the Lessons Learned Analysis with its Five Hows; this source's 5 Whys is a root-cause technique in origin, so use it only under LFUO's anti-causal-statement discipline; TRIZ surfaces system features that resemble the adverse design

findings.claim: OB names "the conformity and attribution-bias dynamics that 1-2-4-Whole Group and Mini Constellations are structurally designed to overcome"
findings.failure_mode: design intent attributed to the LS structures that the handbook does not state
findings.evidence: OB deep ref lines 81, 294 do cover attribution bias and conformity. The handbook deep ref (lines 59, 99) gives 1-2-4's purpose as giving everyone a chance to talk and Mini Constellations' as speaking from a positional "role"; neither is described as designed against conformity, and nothing links either to attribution bias.
findings.fix: correct: OB names the conformity dynamics (Ch 9.2) that 1-2-4-Whole Group and Mini Constellations can help counter by giving every voice a turn; use together when the facilitator needs to name what is happening in the room

findings.claim: "Open Space Technology (Harrison Owen, openspaceworld.org)"

findings.fix: strip: Harrison Owen

findings.claim: "the handbook does not specify which combinations work well for which situations"
findings.failure_mode: limit overstated
findings.evidence: Deep ref line 59: 1-2-4 "can be done on its own or combined with Impromptu Speed Networking"; line 65: Taking Questions after Celebrity Interviews; line 73: Gallery Walk as alternative to report-outs; source line 1439: 15% Solutions "works very well using the Troika process".
findings.fix: correct: the handbook names a few pairings (1-2-4 with Impromptu Speed Networking; Gallery Walk in place of report-outs) but gives no general guide to which combinations suit which situations

notes: Counting: claims_audited counts distinct assertions (relevance sentences, concept sub-claims, table cells, What-to-Look-For diagnosis/follow-up, worked-example steps, anti-patterns, integration rows, integrity-note items); faithful = claims_audited - findings. Every quoted span was compared mechanically against the deep ref and the converted source (curly/straight quotes normalised), then mismatches read by hand. All [V] quotes match the source word for word except D002 (truncation). Every [V] quote is present in the deep ref (the combined DAD closing pair at lines 76 and 111 is two consecutive deep-ref questions). Unmarked verbatim quotes: lines 16, 18, 24, 34. Converted source consulted for Ownership, Nothing About Me, Engage the Unusual Suspects, Wise Crowds, Just In Time Topics, 5 Whys, Impromptu Speed Networking, 1-2-4, DAD, TRIZ, Wicked Questions, 15% Solutions, Troika, Agreement/Uncertainty, 25-to-10, After Action Debrief, Gallery Walk, Mini Constellations, Levels of Accountability. Other deep refs checked for integration claims: tc-25-20-army-aar-deep (AAR vs critique, lines 15, 31-38), lfuo-learning-review-guide-2024-deep (root cause, networked causality, Lessons Learned Analysis / Five Hows, lines 17, 57, 91, 145-160, 306), nhs-just-culture-guide-deep (decision tree, lines 5-60), openstax-organizational-behavior-deep (attribution bias and conformity, lines 81, 294). The 'below-the-line' reading of helplessness (line 95) was left FAITHFUL: the source asks how to work 'above the line' and places 'Somebody should do something' and 'Woe is me' near the bottom, though it does not mark the line's position.
